This walkthrough takes you from zero to a normalized dataset in under
5 minutes using bundled demo data — no external files needed.

<!-- TODO: Record screencast showing full first-analysis workflow -->
<!-- ![First analysis end-to-end](../man/figures/screencasts/first-analysis.gif) -->

<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert">
<strong>Time:</strong> ~5 minutes &nbsp;|&nbsp;
<strong>Prerequisites:</strong> MRMhub installed (<code>check_setup()</code> passes) &nbsp;|&nbsp;
<strong>Data:</strong> Bundled demo (no downloads)
</div>

## Step 1: Load MRMhub

```{r}
library(mrmhub)
```

## Step 2: Import Demo Data

MRMhub ships with a demo dataset produced by INTEGRATOR.
Import it with `import_data_mrmhub()`:

```{r}
demo_file <- system.file("extdata", "MRMhub_demo.tsv", package = "mrmhub")
mexp <- import_data_mrmhub(demo_file)
mexp
```

The result is an `MRMhubExperiment` object — a structured container 
holding your peak area data, sample annotations, and feature metadata.

## Step 3: Explore the Data

```{r}
# Dimensions: samples × features
get_analysis_count(mexp)
get_feature_count(mexp)

# First few sample annotations
head(mexp@annot_analyses)

# Feature list
get_featurelist(mexp)
```

## Step 4: Normalize by Internal Standard

Apply ISTD normalization to correct for extraction and injection variability:

```{r}
mexp <- normalize_by_istd(mexp)
```

<div class="alert alert-success" role="alert">
After this step, <code>mexp@is_istd_normalized</code> is <code>TRUE</code>.
The original data is preserved in <code>dataset_orig</code>.
</div>

## Step 5: Visualise

Check the run sequence for signal drift:

```{r, fig.height=4}
plot_runscatter(mexp, y = "area_normalized")
```

## Step 6: Export

Export the processed data to Excel or CSV:

```{r}
# Excel report (multiple sheets)
save_report_xlsx(mexp, file = "my_first_results.xlsx")

# Or as tidy CSV
save_dataset_csv(mexp, file = "my_first_results.csv")
```
